A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SegQuant work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v5 reports original image-generation benchmarks, component ablations, quantization-error analyses, and runtime measurements in the main text and Appendix B.

after.justification: v7 retains those original results and adds DualScale calibration sensitivity and semantic-segmentation control experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The SegLinear segmentation procedure, DualScale polarity decomposition, optimizer/calibrator framework, and batched-GEMM implementation remain unchanged. Appendix B retains the same graph-detection algorithm; the new experiments test existing components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same image-generation coverage on COCO, MJHQ-30K, and DCI. The new SD3 diagnostic experiments vary calibration and segmentation within existing coverage rather than introduce another task, domain, or test environment.

E2.justification: v7 adds random six-chunk and mismatched eight-chunk comparators against SegLinear in Table 6, and a standard-quantization control in the new DualScale sensitivity comparison in Table 5. Existing benchmark comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New Appendix B protocols evaluate relative Frobenius error at calibration percentiles 1.0, 0.9999, and 0.9990 with calibration sizes 100 and 200, and compare inferred, random, and mismatched segmentation. Existing benchmark sampling, metrics, and calibration budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v7 adds two targeted analyses: whether clipping outliers harms DualScale, and whether semantic alignment improves segmentation beyond arbitrary chunking. Tables 5–6 supplement the retained component ablations and visual analyses without substantially expanding their model coverage.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these comparisons. The new N=100 and N=200 values denote calibration-set sizes, not repeated trials or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: New results include DualScale relative errors of 0.0108/0.0102 at N=100/200 and SegLinear error 0.5415 versus 0.7080 for random and 0.5713 for mismatched chunking. Section 5.2 corrects its quoted FID reduction from 15.28→12.29 to 23.35→22.54, matching the unchanged Table 4. Existing benchmark scores are retained.

T1.justification: The quantization definitions, segmentation equations, DualScale derivation, and Appendix A recovery calculations are unchanged. The new appendix discussion provides empirical interpretations rather than new formal assumptions, propositions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: compiler-compatible SegQuant, automatic graph-based SegLinear, and hardware-native DualScale. The shortened conclusion preserves the central quality and generalization claims without substantively redefining their scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix B discussion interprets clipping sensitivity as evidence that large outliers carry semantic information and argues that modest calibration sets suffice. It also attributes the segmentation advantage to alignment with semantic boundaries rather than arbitrary finer partitioning.

D1.justification: v7 supplies an explicit SegQuant repository URL where v5 only mentioned released code. The main hardware description changes from GPU model names to architecture and VRAM capacities, and Table 3 drops the GPTQ qualifier for SVDQuant without establishing a procedural change. Existing runtime and implementation disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v7 adds a CUTLASS reference for the implementation library already described in v5. The substantive related-work comparisons and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v7 condenses the ablation discussion and conclusion, edits attention terminology and author/correspondence text, and adds acknowledgments and two appendix explanatory subsections. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v7 adds compact appendix Tables 5–6, with former Tables 5–11 becoming Tables 7–13. It compacts the author block, relocates Figure 1 and several tables, and resizes or repositions some figures. Existing visual content and table structures are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The new clipping-sensitivity and segmentation controls modestly strengthen validation of the proposed components. Correcting Section 5.2's inconsistency with Table 4 and providing a concrete code URL improve accuracy and reproducibility information. The added evidence remains limited to SD3 error diagnostics without uncertainty reporting, and Table 3 loses a configuration qualifier, so the overall improvement is useful but limited.
